summary_for_children: At-Tariq means The Night Comer, the piercing star. It reminds us every soul is watched over and swears by the sky that returns rain and the earth that cracks open.
environment_concept: A clear night with one star brighter than the rest, its light sharp and piercing (86:3). Further on, a small cloud keeps returning rain onto a patch of ground (86:11), where the earth cracks open and sprouts push through (86:12). No person is shown.
architecture_and_scenery: A bright star with rays, a rain cloud with falling drops, cracked earth with sprouts.

story_library.title: The Night Visitor
story_library.children_narration: On a clear night, a bright star can catch our attention. Surah At-Tariq begins with an oath by the sky and the night visitor, described as a piercing star. The surah reminds us of human creation and Allah's knowledge.

world_idea.title: The Piercing Star Observatory
world_idea.description: Explore a night-sky learning environment and investigate stars, light, and human development through carefully separated educational exhibits.
